children: Kioxia Holdings has teamed up with Nvidia to expand the amount of data that graphics processing units, or GPUs, can access using the Japanese company's data storage devices.
The Japanese chip maker said Thursday that the collaboration demonstrated how Nvidia software and Kioxia's solid-state drives could extend the effective memory capacity of GPUs.

Kioxia said rapid growth in artificial intelligence datasets is straining the capacity of the high-bandwidth memory that GPUs typically use. The approach could make larger datasets available for AI processing than high-bandwidth memory alone can hold, the company said.
Kioxia said it continues to develop solid-state drives for AI and high-performance computing.
